document_title: EU Regulatory Compliance Requirements for SaaS Providers

gdpr.scope: All companies processing EU resident data

data_protection_officer.required_when: Processing personal data of >250 employees OR high-risk processing
data_protection_officer.reporting: Reports directly to highest management level

lawful_basis.documentation_required: Privacy notices, consent records, legitimate interest assessments

data_subject_rights.access: Provide copy of personal data within 1 month
data_subject_rights.rectification: Correct inaccurate personal data within 1 month
data_subject_rights.erasure: Delete data when no longer necessary (right to be forgotten)
data_subject_rights.portability: Provide data in structured, machine-readable format
data_subject_rights.objection: Allow objection to legitimate interest processing

technical_measures.encryption: Data at rest and in transit

penalties.tier_1: Up to €10M or 2% of global annual revenue
penalties.tier_2: Up to €20M or 4% of global annual revenue

germany.additional_requirements: BDSG (Federal Data Protection Act) supplements GDPR
germany.data_localization: Sensitive government data must remain in Germany
germany.employee_data: Works council consultation required for employee monitoring

france.additional_requirements: Law for a Digital Republic adds specific obligations
france.data_localization: Critical infrastructure data must stay in France
france.language: Privacy notices must be available in French

netherlands.enforcement: Dutch DPA known for proportionate enforcement approach

eu_ai_act.scope: AI systems used in EU market

prohibited.penalty: Up to €35M or 7% global annual revenue

high_risk.penalty: Up to €15M or 3% global annual revenue

limited_risk.penalty: Up to €7.5M or 1.5% global annual revenue

saas_implications.customer_data_analysis: Likely high-risk if used for automated decision making
saas_implications.chatbot_features: Limited risk - must disclose AI interaction
saas_implications.predictive_analytics: Risk level depends on use case and impact

nis2_directive.scope: Essential and important digital service providers

applicability_criteria.essential_entities: >250 employees AND >€50M revenue AND critical sectors
applicability_criteria.important_entities: >50 employees AND >€10M revenue AND digital infrastructure

security_requirements.incident_reporting: 24 hours to national CSIRT, details within 72 hours
security_requirements.risk_management: Cybersecurity risk assessment and management measures
security_requirements.business_continuity: Backup, disaster recovery, and crisis management
security_requirements.supply_chain: Security requirements for suppliers and service providers

penalties.essential_entities: Up to €10M or 2% global annual revenue
penalties.important_entities: Up to €7M or 1.4% global annual revenue

digital_services_act.scope: Digital service providers operating in EU

strict_localization.requirements: Data must be stored and processed locally

technical_implementation.factors: Data encryption, access controls, audit trails

local_data_processing.cost_benefit: Reduced data transfer and compliance costs

entry_strategy: Establish EU entity for GDPR representative requirements
Partner with local legal counsel in target countries
Obtain relevant certifications (ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II)
ongoing_compliance: Continuous staff training on data protection
